extracted.intended_audience: improvisers, improv students, and performers learning UCB long-form techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for practicing and performing long-form comedic improvisation using the Upright Citizens Brigade (UCB) approach, including scene work, game-finding, openings, and longform structures like the Harold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yes, And
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-positioned as only one of two distinct parts of scenework; used to establish a Base Reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Yes And-ing to establish a Base Reality, scene partners move to discover the First Unusual Thing. The book treats 'Yes, And' as necessary but not sufficient, contrasting it with the newer 'If, Then' mantra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base Reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a Base Reality to ground the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters: 'What is a Base Reality?' and 'How to Create a Base Reality.' The Base Reality is created after initial Yes, And moves and provides the factual world from which the scene's unusual elements emerge.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Unusual Thing
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a First Unusual Thing in the scene which becomes the seed for the scene's comedic pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scene partners strive to discover the First Unusual Thing, which is then framed, agreed upon, and developed into a patterned, repeatable Game.

rubrics_metrics.name: If, Then
rubrics_metrics.description: Mantra: 'If this is true, then what else is true?' used to drive scene exploration and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a newer summary of the process that breaks from the tenet of 'Yes, And'; encourages following implications of established facts to generate material and escalate the Game.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game
rubrics_metrics.description: The patterned, repeatable comedic element developed from the First Unusual Thing and agreed-upon framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered across Section II (What is a Game? Finding Game; Playing Game). The Game is the recurring pattern the scene plays, and success is measured by how clearly it is found, framed, and played.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding Game
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques and attention for identifying the central Game in a scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter: 'Finding Game.' Emphasis on noticing unusualness and pattern potential; explicit methods are presented to locate the Game early so ensemble can commit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playing Game
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches for actively playing and committing to the discovered Game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter: 'Playing Game.' Focus is on exploitation of the pattern, escalation, callbacks, and maintaining clarity of the Game for the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Character to Play Game
rubrics_metrics.description: Use strong character choices as a tool to play and escalate the Game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter: 'Using Character to Play Game.' Character work should serve the Game rather than distract; character choices can clarify relationships and stakes that feed the pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Support Moves to Play Game as a Group
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensemble support moves that reinforce and advance the Game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter: 'Using Support Moves to Play Game as a Group.' Emphasizes collaborative moves (offers, tags, confirmations) that keep the Game coherent and escalate collectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helpful Hints & Hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical tips and common pitfalls to avoid in scene work and longform performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter: 'Helpful Hints & Hazards.' The book lists specific dos and don'ts to protect the Game and ensemble choices; intended as pragmatic performance-oriented advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longform Structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Various longform templates and structures for organizing a full show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section III delineates longform forms including a full chapter on the Harold and sections on Movie, Monoscene, Deconstruction, and others; guidance includes how to structure scenes and transitions across a set.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Harold
rubrics_metrics.description: A dedicated longform structure (Harold) with its own chapter of instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter: 'The Harold' (Chapter 11). The Manual provides specific guidance on starting, weaving, and revisiting beats/themes as part of Harold structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASSSSCAT as a distinct form
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of ASSSSCAT as a longform form in its own right, rather than grouping it under Armando/Monologue Deconstruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Manual labels ASSSSCAT as its own form, marking a departure from more common categorizations; guidance implies different expectations and structure for this form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openings (monologues, Pattern Game, Invocation, Character Monologues, Organic Openings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different improvisational openings to launch longform sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter: 'Openings' (Chapter 10). Examples include monologues, the Pattern Game, an Invocation (example: Del Close performing an Invocation of himself), Character Monologues (like Documentary openings), and Organic Openings. Each opening supplies different seed material and tone for the longform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern Game (as an opening technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a Pattern Game at the top to establish recurring beats or motifs for the show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned among openings; Pattern Game can function both as an opening and as a device throughout longform to create recognizable patterns for callbacks and development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting from an Audience Suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique for initiating longform work by soliciting and using an audience suggestion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter: 'Starting from an Audience Suggestion' (Chapter 9). Guidance on how to harvest usable seed material from suggestions and integrate them into openings and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearsal & Performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices for rehearsal and performance tailored to longform improv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter: 'Rehearsal & Performance' (Chapter 13). Covers how to rehearse longform structures, run sets, and prepare as an ensemble for live shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility to Beginners
rubrics_metrics.description: Write and teach in a way that is accessible to people with no prior improv experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors intentionally wrote the book to be accessible to complete newcomers, structuring explanations and chapters to introduce core concepts from fundamentals upward.
